s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling and drainage of serosanguinous fluid from the left labia with signs of sepsis and subcutaneous gas
salient_findings: Progressive swelling of the left labia
Rupture and drainage of serosanguinous fluid
key_facts: Six-day history of progressive swelling of the left labia
Rupture and drainage of serosanguinous fluid two days before admission
Blood pressure 100/60 mmHg despite intravenous fluid resuscitation
Pelvic CT imaging showed ulceration of the left labia with air in the subcutaneous fat
Inflammatory fat stranding along the left lateral abdominal wall
LRINEC score of 3 with potential to rise to 7

shortlist.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of subcutaneous gas on CT and elevated LRINEC score

shortlist.label: Fournier gangrene
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive swelling and drainage of serosanguinous fluid from the left labia

shortlist.label: Gas gangrene
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous gas on CT and signs of sepsis

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Signs of sepsis and elevated white blood cell count

shortlist.label: Severe cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammatory fat stranding along the left lateral abdominal wall and elevated white blood cell count

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with progressive swelling of the left labia, rupture and drainage of serosanguinous fluid, and imaging findings of ulceration and air in the subcutaneous fat of the left groin are consistent with Fournier gangrene, a severe and necrotizing infection of the genital and perineal area.

rejected.label: Necrotizing fasciitis
rejected.why: While the patient has some risk factors and findings suggestive of necrotizing fasciitis, such as the LRINEC score and subcutaneous gas, the specific location and nature of the infection are more consistent with Fournier gangrene.

rejected.label: Gas gangrene
rejected.why: Gas gangrene typically involves muscle tissue and is caused by Clostridium perfringens, whereas the patient's presentation suggests a more superficial and localized infection.

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not suggest a toxic shock syndrome, which typically presents with more severe systemic symptoms and a distinct laboratory profile.

rejected.label: Severe cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has some findings consistent with cellulitis, such as inflammatory fat stranding, the presence of subcutaneous gas and ulceration suggest a more severe and necrotizing infection, such as Fournier gangrene.
